newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dassault wants identity after merger - paper.
newsitem.headline: Dassault wants identity after merger - paper.

text.p: French combat plane maker Dassault Aviation wants to keep its military identity separate from the civilian activities of SNI Aerospatiale following a merger of the two firms, the Dassault chairman said on Thursday.

"If there is a merger between Dassault and Aerospatiale, we must keep the identities of the two branches, as the clients of Airbus and Rafale have nothing in common..." Serge Dassault said in an interview with weekly Paris Match magazine.
Other aircraft firms such as McDonnell Douglas and British Aerospace have kept their military and civilian businesses separate, he added.
Dassault wants to keep the combat plane culture separate from the civilian activities of Aerospatiale, he said.

"I insist that we do not mix up the different cultures in this operation, anyway, it would resisted by the employees of both groups," he said. Keeping a separate cultural identity was important to the maintainance of morale among Dassault staff, he said.
However, the two groups work together on common space, missile and civilian aircraft projects, he said.
Dassault makes the Mirage and Rafale combat planes, as well as the Falcon small business jet.

State-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale is a partner in the Airbus Industrie passenger plane consortium, along with British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
